emma: hitting repeated 413s when we upload large embedding batches to /v1/embeddings/stream. happens only for larger datasets (>50k rows) and intermittently. curl shows: HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large. anyone seen this?

emma: example curl we use (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings/stream \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  --data-binary @big-embeds.json
```

emma: server body: {"error":"request too large","status":413} — no extra hints. we're already chunking on the client by batching 1000 items in one file.

sara (Support): thanks emma — sorry for the pain. a few quick Qs: which model and embedding dim? are you sending a single huge JSON array (e.g., [.., .., ..]) or newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON)? what client lib/language?

emma: using model: text-embed-1536, dim=1536. client: python requests, we write a single file that is a JSON array of 60k embedding objects then stream that file with --data-binary. batch size ~1000 per request.

max (Support-Engineer): sending a single massive JSON array is a common trigger for 413s because reverse proxies and gateways often see a big content-length and reject it. NDJSON streaming or using Transfer-Encoding: chunked usually avoids the body-size checks at the proxy layer. can you try splitting into newline-delimited JSON (one embedding object per line) and stream with chunked? example NDJSON: see below.

max (Support-Engineer): NDJSON example:
```
{"id":"1","input":"..."}
{"id":"2","input":"..."}
{"id":"3","input":"..."}
```

max (Support-Engineer): approximate payload calc: number_of_items * dim * 4 (bytes per float32) + JSON overhead. so 60k * 1536 * 4 ≈ 368MB raw floats before overhead — that explains why the gateway rejects it. even with quantized ints, JSON text expands it more. aim for < ~10MB per HTTP request to be safe (depends on proxy config).

emma: oh wow I assumed batching 1000 would be fine. our JSON overhead killed us. is there a recommended batch size?

sara (Support): safe defaults we recommend: - NDJSON streaming (one object per line) - batch sizes that produce ~2–8MB payloads per request (try batch_size=200 for 1536-dim) - use gzip compression (Content-Encoding: gzip) when possible - if you must send arrays, keep them < ~10k items depending on dim

raj (Eng - Runtime): tagging in case this is a runtime/proxy config issue. can you also paste raw request headers (sanitized) and the first 2KB of request body? that helps us see if Transfer-Encoding or Content-Length is causing proxy to enforce limits. also we'll grep ingress logs for 1753890123 from our gateway.

emma: attaching sanitized headers snippet:
```
POST /v1/embeddings/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: my-client/1.2
```
and the body starts with: `[{"id":"1","input":"...","metadata":{...}},` so yes it's a JSON array.

deploy-bot: noticed 413 spikes for /v1/embeddings/stream from customer emma@acct-47 at 2026-06-11T14:22:03Z — creating incident-logs ticket #INC-4821 for ingress logs retention.

raj (Eng - Runtime): thank you. initial find: our edge nginx has client_max_body_size=10m by default for the stream path and the API gateway also rejects >10MB arrays. chunked/ndjson with Transfer-Encoding usually bypasses the client_max_body_size path because the request isn't accepted as a single big payload. we can increase the limit for dedicated customers but that risks memory spikes. prefer recommending client changes.

max (Support-Engineer): quick repro steps for your team: 1) convert array -> NDJSON 2) stream via requests with chunked transfer: 
```python
import requests
with open('embeds.ndjson','rb') as f:
    r = requests.post(url, headers=headers, data=f)  # requests streams file by default
```
or set headers: {'Transfer-Encoding':'chunked'} with a streaming generator. 3) set Content-Encoding: gzip if you compress. 4) set batch_size ~200 and verify payload bytes < 8MB.

emma: tried NDJSON + gzip + batch_size=200. same dataset now streams through, no 413s after ~12k items. will run full job overnight.

sara (Support): great — can you confirm once finished and we'll close the ticket. if you still see intermittent rejections, please attach raw request captures and the exact timestamp; we can temporarily bump edge limit for your account to test.

emma: confirmed — full run succeeded, no 413s. thanks everyone, NDJSON + gzip + smaller batches did the trick. :tada:

raj (Eng - Runtime): noting action item: evaluate allowing chunked NDJSON explicitly in our docs and add a troubleshooting note about client_max_body_size/10MB default. filing internal doc task DOC-1258.

sara (Support): closing loop here — glad it worked. leaving the incident ticket open for 48h in case of recurrence.
